title: Microservices Decomposition Strategies
description: Learn domain-driven design, bounded contexts, and the strangler fig pattern for decomposing monoliths.

data.text: Decomposing a monolith into microservices requires a strategy. Domain-Driven Design (DDD) provides the vocabulary and patterns for identifying service boundaries. The Strangler Fig pattern provides a safe migration path.

terms.definition: A software design approach that models software to match a business domain.
A boundary within which a particular domain model is defined and consistent.
A migration pattern that gradually replaces a monolith by routing new functionality to new services.
A shared language between developers and domain experts used in code and communication.

data.text: DDD helps you identify service boundaries by modeling the business domain. The key concepts are entities, value objects, aggregates, and bounded contexts. Each bounded context becomes a candidate microservice.

items: A bounded context defines where a domain model applies
Each context has its own ubiquitous language
Contexts are separated by explicit boundaries
Context mapping defines relationships between contexts

rows: Split by how often parts change

data.text: The Strangler Fig pattern replaces a monolith incrementally. New functionality is built as separate services. The monolith is gradually "strangled" as more functionality moves to the new services.

data.caption: Strangler Fig Migration Pattern
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Client[Client] --> GW[API Gateway / Facade]
    GW -->|New features| S1[New Service]
    GW -->|Legacy features| M[Monolith]
    M --> DB1[(Legacy DB)]
    S1 --> DB2[(New DB)]
    S1 -.->|Gradually replace| M

data.title: Exercise: Decompose a Monolith
data.description: Take a sample monolith (e-commerce) and identify bounded contexts using DDD.
steps: Define the ubiquitous language for each context
Propose a strangler fig migration plan
Identify the first context to extract
data.expectedOutcome: A context map with bounded contexts and a migration plan

items.question: What is the difference between DDD and microservices?
items.answer: DDD is a design approach; microservices is an architecture. DDD helps you find microservice boundaries.

items.question: What is a bounded context?
items.answer: A boundary within which a domain model is defined and consistent. It is the primary unit of decomposition in DDD.

items.question: How do you start a strangler fig migration?
items.answer: Start with a small, low-risk bounded context. Build the new service, route traffic, and remove the old code.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DDD provides the vocabulary for service boundaries
Bounded contexts are the primary unit of decomposition
Strangler fig enables safe incremental migration
data.takeaway: Use DDD to identify boundaries and the strangler fig pattern to migrate safely.
